Mapping Our Shared History: Introducing the National Preservation Atlas

Unknown Sara Bronin historic preservation, atlas, georeferencing, legal geography, public data
Read the source article

Quick summary

The National Preservation Atlas aims to turn fragmented historic-preservation records into a searchable national map that links places, legal protections, and public policy.

Key takeaways

  • Sara Bronin’s essay introduces the National Preservation Atlas (NPA) as an ambitious attempt to consolidate and map historic-preservation data across the United States.
  • The article emphasizes that the NPA is not only mapping places; it is also mapping the legal and regulatory regimes attached to them.
  • A major theme of the piece is data quality and standardization.
  • The essay also suggests that the atlas can change preservation from a reactive discipline into a proactive one.
  • Finally, Bronin highlights the narrative and political dimension.
